# Fixture surfaces

Each file is a captured `tools/list` built around one specific way an MCP surface becomes
unreadable to a model. They are the basis of the tests and the demo material for the
README, which is why every one of them documents the failure it provokes.

None of these is a real server. Nothing here is ever executed — see `tests/non-execution.test.ts`.

| File                             | The mistake                                                                                                                                                                                           | What it should produce                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `list-search-pair.json`          | `list_users` and `search_users` share a byte-identical description; only the schema distinguishes them.                                                                                               | `descriptions/identical` (error) and a top overlap pair. The classic case: the model has to guess from parameter names.                                                                                                                          |
| `get-fetch-pair.json`            | `get_document`, `fetch_document` and `read_document` are three names for one operation, with near-identical descriptions and only the parameter name differing.                                       | High `overlap/high` scores across all three pairs. A three-way confusion is worse than a two-way one because no single rename fixes it.                                                                                                          |
| `inconsistent-prefixes.json`     | Four naming conventions on one surface: `docs_list`, `listFolders`, `folder-get`, `Search.In.Documents`.                                                                                              | Low overlap but no usable pattern for the model to generalise from; the fixture exists to show that lexical overlap does _not_ catch this, which is the point of measuring confusion for real.                                                   |
| `no-annotations.json`            | A surface with a destructive `delete_branch` and no annotations anywhere.                                                                                                                             | `annotations/absent-surface-wide` (warning). Clients apply the documented defaults — not read-only, potentially destructive, not idempotent, open-world — to every tool, including the harmless reads.                                           |
| `copied-descriptions.json`       | The same placeholder description pasted onto three unrelated tools, one of which sends email.                                                                                                         | `descriptions/identical` (error) on every pair. The worst case in the set: nothing in the text separates a read from an outbound message.                                                                                                        |
| `contradictory-annotations.json` | `readOnlyHint: true` together with `destructiveHint: true`; a `delete_workspace` that declares `destructiveHint: false`; an `update_settings` that claims to be read-only; an invented `cachingHint`. | `annotations/contradictory-read-only-destructive` (error), `annotations/destructive-name-declared-safe` (warning), `annotations/read-only-with-mutating-name` (warning), `annotations/unknown-key` (info).                                       |
| `refs-and-defs.json`             | `$defs` with a nested ref, a self-recursive category tree, and an external `$ref` to another host.                                                                                                    | Refs inline for analysis; the recursive one is reported as a cycle and left alone; the external one is reported as external. The wire schema — and therefore the token count — is unchanged by any of it.                                        |
| `bloated.json`                   | One tool whose description and enum dominate the surface's token budget.                                                                                                                              | `query_analytics` holding the large majority of the context cost, which is the number to look at before adding a fourth tool.                                                                                                                    |
| `header-params.json`             | Three `x-mcp-header` annotations: one valid, one on a `number` parameter with a space in the header name, one buried under `items`.                                                                   | One `x-mcp-header/present` info note and two `x-mcp-header/invalid` errors. The two invalid tools are excluded from `tools/list` by any conforming Streamable HTTP client, so the model sees a one-tool server where the maintainer wrote three. |
| `clean.json`                     | Nothing. Distinct names, distinct descriptions, complete and consistent annotations.                                                                                                                  | Zero errors and zero warnings. A tool that flags this surface is crying wolf, so `tests/inspect.test.ts` asserts it stays quiet.                                                                                                                 |
| `jsonrpc-envelope.json`          | Not a mistake: the same tool list wrapped in a full JSON-RPC response.                                                                                                                                | Exercises the snapshot transport's envelope handling.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `malformed.json`                 | A duplicate tool name, an entry with no name, a non-string description, a tool with no `inputSchema`, and a bare string in the array.                                                                 | One diagnostic per problem, and a surface that still loads: a broken entry must not take the whole inspection down.                                                                                                                              |
